$comment: The one home of villanelle's API concepts, members, kind lists, error groups, limits and reserved names (spec/spec.md and spec/contract.md are canonical for behaviour; this file is canonical for the lists). Names are spec names: lowercase words; a binding changes only the casing (spec/binding-guide.md rule 1) except where a member's 'spell' records an allowed difference. 'ts' and 'py' give each binding's spelling after milestone 4 (beads vil-umh.1 to vil-umh.8 and vil-umh.12; .claude/design/consumer-api/round15/frozen-m4.md; earlier milestones: round14/frozen-m1.md to frozen-m3.md). A concept with 'variants' is a union over a kind list ('kind list', less any 'except'): its members are the ones every variant has. Each variant concept names its union in 'variant of' and its kind value in 'kind', and lists only the members it adds; it has every member of its union too. 'extends' names a concept of a lower layer whose members it also has. 'py module' names the only Python module that exports a type when that is not the package root. Every member is present in every binding: there is no deferral marker (tools/gen-api.py --check refuses one).

naming.rule: The spec names each concept once in plain lowercase words; each binding only changes the casing.

ts.type: PascalCase; interfaces keep an I prefix until the owner answers binding-guide rule 2
ts.kind value: the lowercase string itself, typed by the list's generated string-literal type
ts.constant: UPPER_SNAKE_CASE (limits, reserved names, patterns); DiagnosticCode keeps a PascalCase-keyed constant object (codes are not words)

py.kind value: StrEnum member UPPER_SNAKE_CASE whose value is the lowercase string

layers.name: shared
layers.holds: positions, places, origins, diagnostics and the diagnostics sink, error groups, the kind lists

layers.name: io
layers.holds: the document source and writer ports, their adapters, and check lost updates (the one lost-update check every writer calls)

layers.name: written
layers.holds: the low level: processor, document graph, documents, statements, values, variables, the expansion and its expanded values with their readers, the extension port and the include extension (spec 5: an extension is pure, so it belongs to the layer that owns expansion)

layers.name: rendered
layers.holds: the rendered tree: render (graph), directives, arguments, addresses, diff

layer direction: A layer imports only the layers in its 'may import' list. Nothing below the rendered layer imports, names or returns a rendered type (owner, 2026-10-29: "The low level shouldn't \"depend on\" the middle layer — they should have different domain objects. The middle layer of objects can build on the lower layer domains"). Going up a layer is the upper layer's free function: render (graph). Each binding enforces this with a check (frozen-m1.md).

error groups.name: villanelle error
error groups.raised when: never by itself: the base class of every expected-outcome class (spec 2.8), so one except or catch clause catches every outcome the input or the outside world decides, and no program bug

error groups.name: diagnostic error
error groups.raised when: a reader is given a value of the wrong kind or spelling, or a program's error(...); carries one located diagnostic as 'diagnostic'

error groups.name: read error
error groups.raised when: load cannot resolve the root path to exactly one file, or cannot read it. No diagnostic and no code
error groups.cause: the source's failure; absent when the source resolved no file or several

error groups.name: bad text error
error groups.raised when: the text given to an edit, or an override's text, is not what its entry rule (spec 2.8) and the text-alone rules take; 'diagnostics' are located in that text, in the binding's string unit; its message is built from them (spec 2.8)

error groups.name: lost update error
error groups.raised when: a file the save would write changed since it was read or last saved: its current text differs from its saved text (spec 4.2). Raised by check lost updates inside every writer; save raises it as is
error groups.note: paths are only the conflicting files, in batch order

error groups.name: detached error
error groups.raised when: any member but kind of a detached handle is used
error groups.py: DetachedError (subclass of ReferenceError, the error a dead weakref proxy raises; not under VillanelleError)

error groups.name: argument type error
error groups.raised when: an argument of the wrong type: anything but text where villanelle text is taken (spec 6.9), a writer that is not a document writer, a key rule that returns anything but text or absent (spec 7.4)

error groups.name: misuse error
error groups.raised when: a bad argument value a program could have checked: every bad name (a variable or override name not matching the variable name pattern, a directive rename the nameText entry rule refuses or that is reserved or an extension's name), a program code without '/', a reserved or repeated extension name

error groups.name: index out of range
error groups.raised when: an insert index outside a block; a token range outside a parse

argument type error message.rule: One helper per binding builds it (one home); every member that takes villanelle text, quote, rename, set override and each load override call it before changing anything. Messages are for people (spec 2.3); the class and the member and parameter named are the contract.
argument type error message.ts: `${member}(): argument "${parameter}" must be a string, not ${got}; villanelle edits take text: quote() a program string, String() a number`
argument type error message.py: f"{member}() argument '{parameter}' must be str, not {type(value).__name__}; villanelle edits take text: quote() a program string, str() a number"
argument type error message.member: the member in the binding's casing, as the caller wrote it: set, replaceWithText / replace_with_text, insertStatements / insert_statements, addStatements / add_statements, insertBefore / insert_before, insertAfter / insert_after, setOverride / set_override, rename, quote, load
argument type error message.parameter: text; name for rename and for set override's name; overrides["<name>"] for a load override
argument type error message.example py: TypeError: set() argument 'text' must be str, not int; villanelle edits take text: quote() a program string, str() a number
argument type error message.example ts: TypeError: set(): argument "text" must be a string, not number; villanelle edits take text: quote() a program string, String() a number

other.example py: TypeError: save() argument 'writer' must be a document writer (an object with a write method), not function

concepts.name: expanded value
concepts.note: a union: one value after expansion ($name replaced) with its links to the lines it came through. The low level owns it (spec 2.9, 6.10): an extension use holds it, a directive expansion's values are it, and a rendered directive's values are the same objects (milestone 4 collapsed value expansion and the rendered argument family into it). The readers stay on every variant: a value of the wrong kind is a problem in the config text, reported as E4002. Two expanded values are equal exactly when their texts are equal (spec 2.9; Python ==)

layer check.rule: two checks, both allow-lists (owner, 2026-10-29). Down: no module outside the rendered layer and the package entry point imports the rendered layer, type-only imports included. Public: the rendered layer reaches the low level only through its public API (document graph expand () and the public types), never a package-internal module or member
layer check.ts: ESLint in ts/eslint.config.js. Down: core no-restricted-imports, files src/**/*.ts, ignores src/rendered/**, src/index.ts, src/**/*.test.ts; pattern group **/rendered and **/rendered/**. Public: files src/rendered/**/*.ts, ignores src/**/*.test.ts; no-restricted-imports pattern group **/written/* with !**/written/index.js (the low level's public entry, new), and no-restricted-syntax refusing a cast through unknown (TSAsExpression with a TSUnknownKeyword type, and a TSAsExpression inside another)
layer check.py: py/tests/test_layers.py, ast scan. Down: every module under src/villanelle/ except villanelle/rendered/** and villanelle/__init__.py fails on import villanelle.rendered[...], from villanelle.rendered[...] import, from villanelle import rendered, or the relative equivalents, TYPE_CHECKING blocks included. Public: every module under villanelle/rendered/ imports the low level only as 'from villanelle.written import <name>' with the name in villanelle.written.__all__ (no submodule, no name starting with _), and reads no attribute starting with one _ (dunders aside) on anything but self or cls, getattr with such a literal included

kind rule: A list whose members have different members or operations is a variant set ('variants': one type per value, each with kind typed by the list). A list whose members share one shape is a tag ('tag of': one type, whose kind or reason field is typed by the list). Every list is generated: TypeScript a string-literal union type, Python a StrEnum (spec/codegen.md).

error fields.rule: read error, save error and lost update error have the same field 'paths' (text[]); read error and save error also chain a cause, the language's own mechanism (TypeScript Error cause, Python __cause__)
error fields.read error paths: the root path as given to load, alone
error fields.save error paths: the resolved paths handed to the writer, in batch order
error fields.lost update error paths: only the files whose current text differs from their saved text, in batch order
